extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and readers interested in research integrity and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: A news article reporting on papers retracted for plagiarism, describing publisher/editor actions, affected authors' responses, and suggested penalties and procedural shortcomings. Highlights standards and practices for handling plagiarism and retractions in academic publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism constitutes severe abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The retraction notices call the plagiarism a “severe abuse of the scientific publishing system.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat plagiarism as a grave violation that justifies retraction of published articles; language in notices should reflect the seriousness (e.g., calling it 'severe abuse').

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of corrective action (prompt retraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals and publishers should act promptly to retract articles when plagiarism is evident; delays are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece criticizes more-than-year-long inaction after an editor promised retractions, noting delays allowed the plagiarized papers to accumulate additional citations. Prompt editorial/publisher action reduces harm, including preventing further citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility to prevent plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should put effort into avoiding plagiarism rather than waiting for authors to report it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors quoted recommend proactive measures (screening/prevention) by journals to detect plagiarism pre- or post-publication instead of relying solely on complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial support for retraction decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors (e.g., editor-in-chief) should support retraction when evidence of plagiarism is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the editor-in-chief supported retraction from the beginning — editorial backing should be explicit to expedite corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher transparency and communication about delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should be transparent about the status and timing of retractions and explain delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elsevier told Retraction Watch the retractions were submitted during a busy period and there were delays; clear communication about reasons for delay and progress is expected to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use admission of wrongdoing to inform process
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's admission of plagiarism should be factored into and can expedite retraction proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the author admitted the plagiarism in emails seen by Retraction Watch; where admission exists, journals/publishers should move decisively rather than delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and penalties for plagiarists
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals/publishers should consider penalties such as temporary bans on authors who commit plagiarism, potentially across multiple journals from the same publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quoted victim recommended further penalties, including temporary bans from both the specific journal and other journals by the same publisher — suggests cross-journal sanctions as deterrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of authors' prior retraction history
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's history of previous retractions for plagiarism is relevant and should influence handling of new cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports the author previously had two other articles retracted for plagiarism; repeat offenders warrant increased scrutiny and possibly stronger sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and discovery (retraction databases / reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be mechanisms for discovering and reporting retractions (and for the public to notify databases when a retraction is missing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction Watch invites readers to let them know if a retraction is not in their database — implying the importance of comprehensive retraction records and public reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing downstream harm (preventing accrual of citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Speedy action on retractions helps prevent plagiarized papers from accumulating more citations, which propagates the harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Victims noted the plagiarized papers accrued about two dozen new citations during the delay; timely retraction is part of limiting the spread and impact of invalid/abusive work.
